title: Administrative Law
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze agencies in the constitutional structure, delegation, appointments and removal, procedural due process, rulemaking and adjudication under the APA, the availability and scope of judicial review, review of legal questions after Loper Bright, the major questions doctrine, and open-government laws.
primary_reading: Cornell LII: the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. chapter 5)

weeks.4: Procedural due process: Mathews v. Eldridge
weeks.7: Availability of review: standing, ripeness and exhaustion
weeks.8: Scope of review: substantial evidence and arbitrary-and-capricious review
weeks.9: Questions of law after Loper Bright
weeks.10: The major questions doctrine and Skidmore
weeks.12: The Freedom of Information Act and open government

blocks.deliverable: Apply the Mathews balancing test to a benefits termination.
Decide whether an agency needed notice and comment.
Week 7 midterm; review an agency action under State Farm.
Predict how a court will review an agency's statutory interpretation.
Draft a FOIA request and analyze an exemption claim.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Regulatory challenge: for a supplied agency rule written for the course, write a comment letter during rulemaking and then a 2,000-word memo on the strongest grounds for judicial review.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
